items.stem: A workload must buffer tasks so a slow consumer can process them later with retries. Which service fits best?

options.rationale: Correct: SQS is a durable queue that buffers messages for later processing with retries.
SNS pushes to subscribers and does not store messages for polling.
CloudFront is a CDN, not a message queue.

items.stem: Which TWO improve reliability when consuming from an SQS queue? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Set the visibility timeout longer than the processing time
options.rationale: Correct: a longer visibility timeout prevents duplicate processing before completion.

options.text: Configure a dead-letter queue for poison messages
options.rationale: Correct: a DLQ isolates messages that repeatedly fail.

options.text: Assume messages are never delivered more than once
options.rationale: Standard queues are at-least-once; consumers must handle duplicates.

options.text: Delete the message before processing completes
options.rationale: Deleting early risks losing work if processing fails.

items.explanation: Correct: Set the visibility timeout longer than the processing time, Configure a dead-letter queue for poison messages.

items.stem: Which service is designed to route events by pattern to many AWS and SaaS targets?

options.rationale: Correct: EventBridge routes events to targets based on event patterns.
FIFO queues provide ordered delivery to consumers, not pattern routing.
Route 53 is DNS, not event routing.
Billing is unrelated to event routing.
